Yarona Going Nowhere

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It took over 17 years for the Rustenburg city council to complete a rapid bus system for the city, and five billion Rand later, the buses are more of a nuisance than a relief.

Unique Selling Point:
17 years, 5 billion Rand, 3 mayors and 22 taxi associations; what's going on with Rustenburg rapid bus system ?

Summary:
Stations collapsed and vandalised, windows broken and cables nicked, weeds growing through the cracks of concrete bus routes and buses too big for the lanes. Speed buses… causing traffic jams during rush hour, going nowhere, transporting no one. The Rustenburg Yarona Rapid bus service is a joke to local residents that have given up on the idea of ever having a speed bus system at their doorstep. Although, no one is laughing when reminded of the more than 3 billion Rand of taxpayers money that the project soaked up. Now, the Rustenburg city council has come to an agreement with taxi bosses, to pay each driver on affected routes 1.3 million Rand, whether the buses are running or not.

Further information:
The Rustenburg municipality in the Northwest province is running large public campaigns to create awareness and market their rapid bus system, Yarona. But there are only four buses, and they are too big for the roads that were built to carry them. There are also no stations from where passengers can buy tickets and get on or off a bus.
Thousands of people live on the outskirts of Rustenburg and many travels from Tlabane, Phokeng, Freedom Park, Sun city and surrounding towns to Rustenburg for work. The Yarona rapid bus network, a similar concept to the Rea Vaya in Johannesburg was supposed to be completed in time for the 2010 soccer world cup. Construction started in 2007.
Five billion Rand and 15 years later and it is still not completed. Bizarrely, Rustenburg city council advertises routes that do not exist. People who have been waiting for the system to be completed, have no hope that they will ever receive this speed service and still rely on taxis. It has become a laughing matter for the communities it was intended to serve. For years there was no transparency on the books to show how the 5 billion was spent and now the municipality is asking national government for 2 billion Rand more. The project was never treated inside the municipality, as an official portfolio matter. Instead, the former mayor, who has been suspended, appointed a director of transport in charge of the project. This was an acting role that was legally only permissible to be filled, for three months. But he has been in this position for seven years now. He instated sub committees to run the project and procure service providers. The role that members in all the sub committees were to play, are not clear. One of these committees is headed by the local taxi association and has only taxi drivers as members. They are all paid a weekly meeting fee of R2000 per person to attend meeting concerning Yarona. This is only one example of how taxpayer’s money is being misspent on the project and they are still asking for more.
This is a serious news story of corruption and mismanagement of state funds but is also tongue in cheek and that is the suggested narrative. If our presenter can take map and a ride to all the stations that were supposed to be built, they will find that only three stations appear to be operational, although it is only by the looks of it. If he takes a ride across the network, he will end up walking between stations, because buses cannot possibly drive on the road network built for this purpose. The stations that cost millions to build, are mere deconstructed shading nets hanging on to vandalized frames. Is this another failure of the department of transport to provide affordable public transport? Or Fikile Mbalula’s department not doing enough to fight back against the taxi industry that does not want the buses around? Is that why nothing is being done to curb corruption and stop the vandalization of the network?


Extra Budget Items:
One night accommodation in Rustenburg for four people.
Travel allowance.

Mr. Lesiba Kekana
Mr. Obed Molele Director of Roads Rustenburg
Mr. Luan Snyders CNLL

Rustenburg
Tlabane

Reason for hidden camera: on Monday 5 September, we will take a ride on the buses and film the route and whether there are any commuters. On Tuesday 6 September we have booked an official ride which we will be allowed to film. We would like to compare the two days...

Script:


YARONA FINAL SCRIPT

OPENING:
FAST PACED SYNOPSIS

UPSOUND
SECURITY GUARD RUNS AWAY

VO
We’re often chased away by security guards when trying to film unannounced.

UPSOUND
FILE:
“I’m telling you, you are not allowed”

VO
So imagine our surprise when, in Rustenburg, a security guard runs away when we ask what her job is.

UPSOUND
TELL US WHAT YOU ARE SUPPOSED TO BE LOOKING AFTER?
“I am looking after this brick and also this yard”


VO
These bricks are what's left of a bus station; part of the town's rapid transport system, Yarona.

SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“What we have here in Rustenburg is our very own SAA”

VO
It’s taken fourteen years and nearly three and a half billion Rands to get here: a rapid transport system that's anything but rapid.

STORY STARTS
PACE CHANGE

VO
Despite the billions already spent, the Rustenburg municipality is now asking for more. The vision? Affordable fast-lane buses similar to Johannesburg’s Rea Vaya, which has been operating for just over 12 years. Here, though, things are happening at a much slower pace.
“We are going to pour taxpayers and rate payers money into this project for the foreseeable future”
VO
Long time resident Cheryl Phillips, is a DA member of Parliament.

SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“The concept started out in 2008. It was scheduled to start out in 2014 and 2014 became 2016 that became 2017 that became 2020 that became 2021”

VO
Then, in July this year, came a high level visit by Transport Minister, Fikile Mbalula. He demanded an urgent forensic audit into how the municipal grants have been spent.

SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“National government provided the money but did not do the oversight. And it was left to the municipality”
VO
Obed Molele has been Acting as the project’s head for ten years.
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
DEREK REVERSAL: You’ve spent 3.4 billion can you say where it has gone?
“We built, and continuedly reinforce concrete bus lanes running on two corridors, that infrastructure does not come cheap, with a concrete.”
VO
That may be an understatement, especially for infrastructure, reinforced or not, that’s unfinished and vandalized. Soon after the Minister’s visit, the first buses hit the road.
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
“We still need to complete the stations and the bus lanes are complete. It is important to emphasise that the BRT lanes are complete”.

VO
Molele agreed to take us on a guided tour of his prized transport system in early September, but we decided to check things out ourselves a day earlier.
UPSOUND
DEREK: “Good Afternoon!”
Heading downtown, we found this makeshift ticketing station and just one of the ten buses Molele says are operational.
LINK
“We are on an official media tour tomorrow, but we thought we’d have a little sneak peek today. Virtually no passengers. Bus lanes aren’t ready yet, so this bus is taking up a lot of space on the road”

VO
In town, the bus uses its specially designated fast lane for only a few kilometres. Just outside the CBD, only the general lane is an option.
LET THE VO BREATHE SO YOU CAN SEE THE ISSUE....
On the outskirts it makes do with narrow, rutted village roads, where it adds to congestion and holds up the municipal Bojanala Bus Service.
But at least the Yarona lanes aren’t completely idle.
LINK
“You may say its billions wasted but pedestrians, cyclists, even motorists are having a ball”
VO
The buses, unable to use lanes that are neglected and unusable, pass stations that are unfinished or sometimes in a state of ruin.
PAUSE
Our official tour begins with a warm welcome from Molele and his colleagues. Together, we wait 25 minutes for a bus.
PAUSE
Finally the bus arrives - it's the same one we were on the day before. The driver takes another 25 minutes to do a painstaking inspection. All the while, Molele insists the fast lanes are working and the buses are running on time.
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
“All the bus lanes are complete”
DEREK: But I think some of them need to be repaired.
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
“No, it is very good high material that we have used. They don’t get potholes”
VO
Once again, with virtually no passengers onboard, traffic builds up in our wake. Packed taxis speed by...as well as a number of municipal Bojanala buses - heading for the same areas as Yarona - and beyond.
PAUSE
Taxi bosses say, the Yarona buses are redundant. Lesiba Kekana speaks for one of the town's largest taxi associations, representing just under 600 taxis.
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANE: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“Rustenburg is a one road or two Road Town, so definitely it did not need that, but our government is our government, what are you gonna tell them?”
VO
The big questions is, with ample public transport already serving Rustenburg, why is the government happy to continue funding this multi-billion Rand project?
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANA: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“If taxi industry has been given a free hearing from the beginning by now the taxi industry should have been an industry that is subsidized by government. But no. Instead, they are coming with their own system of transport that will get rid of the black person’s transport”
VO
Ironically, Molele says Yarona was needed because the taxis cause congestion.
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
“If you look at the taxi rank it is excessively full in fact the fleet itself is overspilling to other parts of the city. So, we cannot continue to increase the number of taxi fleet in our”
VO
Government must now pay the losses the taxi industry may incur. Taxis are removed from the Yarona routes to stimulate the market for buses. A lucrative solution for some taxi owners.. but crippling for the taxpayer.
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANE: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“They have removed almost 80% of the taxis on the road and all those owners whose taxis have been removed are then compensated by the so-called loss of income of 11900…
DEREK REVERSAL: Per month?
“Ja per month, per car, the car per operating license. Say maybe Ive got two or three cars, I will get that 11900 times the vehicles that I had”
VO
It’s a cushy arrangement for the bosses it seems, but hasn’t gone down well with the drivers- as we discover on a visit to the rank.
UPSPOUND
“This thing of the project of the RRT, they have been talking to the association, but they have never talked to the drivers”
UPSOUND
“What about us drivers cause, the owners they got some small money”
DEREK REVERSAL: And they haven’t worked out a package for you?”
“No”
DEREK: Only for the bosses?

VO
In fact, the owners have even more say than the drivers might think. In the local council, affected parties have formed sub-committees to steer Yarona, and a number of taxi bosses serve on one of these.
SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“Arrangements and allocations are discussed in the sub committees and the sub committees don’t report back to the portfolio committee and they don’t report back to council. So, it happens in the subcommittee and the DA has no representatives on the sub committees.
DEREK REVERSAL: WHY NOT?
“We’ve asked and we were told it is not a function of council”
VO
140 taxi owners get the monthly compensation - costing the ratepayers at least 20-million rand a year. But it doesn't end there: more than a thousand taxis are still to be removed and their owners have negotiated an increased rate.
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANE: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“Every vehicle with an operating license, the agreement is that they should be given one point three million to exit the industry
DEREK REVERSAL: One point three million
“Per operating license. Say, as Lesiba, I have got 5 taxis, when they get me out of the road, they must give me that 6.5 million that is 1.3 times 5.
DEREK REVERSAL: That is a lot of money
“It is but our government says they do have that budget so let’s see.
DEREK REVERSAL: So that money is being claimed even before the buses are even running here.
“Ja at the moment, that buses are not running in our route”


VO
Flanked by two taxi bosses during our interview, Molele says Yarona has now asked for an additional one and a half billion Rand to settle negotiations with the associations. Only 200 million will be spent on fixing the infrastructure. But what about the day to day operational costs?
SUPER@ OBED MOLELE: ACTING DIRECTOR: ROADS AND TRANSPORT: RLM
DEREK REVERSAL: Do you really think Yarona can pay for itself?
“We can at least recover up to 40% to 50% of our operational overheads. The balance would then have to be subsidized by national government”
VO
With no commuters, it will be challenging to finance the operation. And extended subsidies mean the municipality will again be knocking on National Treasury’s door. This while scores of taxi drivers are losing their jobs.
PAUSE
SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“I cant see it working in Rustenburg. We only got a small percentage of the taxi drivers on board and if I look at the violence that’s erupting for buses in other parts of the country, what is going to happen here in Rustenburg? I don’t see it ending well”


__________________________________________________________________________

PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO
14 years, 3 mayors and 3.4 billion Rand later. And this is the rapid bus system of the Rustenburg municipality.
SUPER@ CHERYL PHILLIPS: MP: DA
“What we have here in Rustenburg is our very own SAA.
UPSOUND DEREK
“Is it ineptitude or straight corruption, a mixture of both? Either way it is one of the craziest sceams Ive seen, working on Carte Blanche”

PROMO 2
DEREK UPSOUND
“15 years in the making, billions wasted, why are they calling it a rapid transport system?”
VO
Rustenburg in the North West launched a rapid bus system, residents don’t see much purpose for it.
UPSOUND
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANE: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“ Rustenburg is a one road or two road town, so it did not need that, but our government is our government, what are you gonna tell them?”


PROMO 2
DEREK UPSOUND
“Taxis are the lifeblood of our transport system and between the violence and the strikes, it does work. So, why on earth does Rustenburg need a rapid transport system, it is beyond me…”
VO
But the system has launched and it leaves little hope for taxi drivers.
SUPER@ LESIBA KEKANE: BAMTA TAXI ASSOCIATION
“Those drivers are sitting without jobs”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It took over 17 years for the Rustenburg city council to complete a rapid bus system for the city, and five billion Rand later, the buses are more of a nuisance than a relief.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: 17 years, 5 billion Rand, 3 mayors and 22 taxi associations; what's going on with Rustenburg rapid bus system ?
metadata.Summary: Stations collapsed and vandalised, windows broken and cables nicked, weeds growing through the cracks of concrete bus routes and buses too big for the lanes. Speed buses… causing traffic jams during rush hour, going nowhere, transporting no one. The Rustenburg Yarona Rapid bus service is a joke to local residents that have given up on the idea of ever having a speed bus system at their doorstep. Although, no one is laughing when reminded of the more than 3 billion Rand of taxpayers money that the project soaked up. Now, the Rustenburg city council has come to an agreement with taxi bosses, to pay each driver on affected routes 1.3 million Rand, whether the buses are running or not.
metadata.Further information: The Rustenburg municipality in the Northwest province is running large public campaigns to create awareness and market their rapid bus system, Yarona. But there are only four buses, and they are too big for the roads that were built to carry them. There are also no stations from where passengers can buy tickets and get on or off a bus. Thousands of people live on the outskirts of Rustenburg and many travels from Tlabane, Phokeng, Freedom Park, Sun city and surrounding towns to Rustenburg for work. The Yarona rapid bus network, a similar concept to the Rea Vaya in Johannesburg was supposed to be completed in time for the 2010 soccer world cup. Construction started in 2007. Five billion Rand and 15 years later and it is still not completed. Bizarrely, Rustenburg city council advertises routes that do not exist. People who have been waiting for the system to be completed, have no hope that they will ever receive this speed service and still rely on taxis. It has become a laughing matter for the communities it was intended to serve. For years there was no transparency on the books to show how the 5 billion was spent and now the municipality is asking national government for 2 billion Rand more. The project was never treated inside the municipality, as an official portfolio matter. Instead, the former mayor, who has been suspended, appointed a director of transport in charge of the project. This was an acting role that was legally only permissible to be filled, for three months. But he has been in this position for seven years now. He instated sub committees to run the project and procure service providers. The role that members in all the sub committees were to play, are not clear. One of these committees is headed by the local taxi association and has only taxi drivers as members. They are all paid a weekly meeting fee of R2000 per person to attend meeting concerning Yarona. This is only one example of how taxpayer’s money is being misspent on the project and they are still asking for more. This is a serious news story of corruption and mismanagement of state funds but is also tongue in cheek and that is the suggested narrative. If our presenter can take map and a ride to all the stations that were supposed to be built, they will find that only three stations appear to be operational, although it is only by the looks of it. If he takes a ride across the network, he will end up walking between stations, because buses cannot possibly drive on the road network built for this purpose. The stations that cost millions to build, are mere deconstructed shading nets hanging on to vandalized frames. Is this another failure of the department of transport to provide affordable public transport? Or Fikile Mbalula’s department not doing enough to fight back against the taxi industry that does not want the buses around? Is that why nothing is being done to curb corruption and stop the vandalization of the network?
